static_traits.name: Chen Feng
static_traits.family_status: Both parents are Teachers; younger sister is a member of a Grunge band
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive friends and colleagues, but has not yet shared financial unease with them; somewhat avoids socializing involving finance/property topics
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy; never had similar financial insecurity before
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, fairly logical, can describe concrete situations and evidence; thinking leans negative with absolutist language (such as 'forever' and 'impossible'); emotions mainly Anxiety and hopelessness; Good cooperation, neutral-to-low tone

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling overwhelmed from worrying that working at the coffee shop will never afford buying a house; worries about financial insecurity have intensified in recent months amid rising housing prices and costs, especially noticeable when Receiving one's paycheck or thinking about future financial stability.
basic_info.core_demands: Ongoing worries about financial stability and being unable to buy a house have affected mental health and daily functioning; hoping to ease Anxiety through counseling, improve functioning, and gradually form more balanced views and feasible small-step actions.

core_beliefs: I am not capable enough to earn enough money
My situation is a dead end, unable to change

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If current income cannot cover high housing prices, the future will not change either; I will never afford a house in this lifetime
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Gains a sense of control through strict budgeting and repeatedly checking expenditures
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This salary means I will never afford a house in this lifetime

special_situations.event: Sees friends or colleagues planning to buy a house / invest in real estate
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not reached my peers' financial milestones, it means I am inferior and a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids socializing involving financial and real-estate topics, reduces contact with friends to avoid comparison
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never catch up with them; I am just not capable

special_situations.event: Notices housing prices and living costs in the city keep rising
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the external environment keeps worsening, no amount of effort will help
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently follows housing price information, falls into worry and reduces long-term planning
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Housing prices will keep rising; I am even less likely to afford it

special_situations.event: Job hunting or interviews not yet resulting in an offer
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Every failure proves I am not good enough, and I will not succeed in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-denial, returning to the original position to maintain the status quo, lowering expectations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not qualified enough; I will never find better Work

core_conflict.wish: Longs to obtain economic security and a decent life (including stable income and buying a house) and a recognized sense of achievement
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure and appearing inferior after being compared with peers, worrying about losing control over the future
defense_goal: Maintaining Self-protection to avoid shame and judgment (avoiding finance topics, Reduced socializing)
Lowering expectations through rationalization and Self-denial, reducing the pain of being frustrated again

object_relations.self_representation: Trapped, with insufficient ability, someone lagging behind peers
object_relations.object_representation: Others (friends / colleagues) are successful people and potential judges

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites considering more balanced evidence, proposing alternative viewpoints or positive affirmations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing optimism as unrealistic, believing that ignoring the harsh reality will lead to greater disappointment
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing objective data such as housing prices and income gaps in a calm, analytical tone, reducing the expression of emotional words and subjective feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing experiences such as job-hunting setbacks or interview rejections
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing failure entirely internally to 'I am not good enough', ignoring external factors like circumstances and competition
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming sentence patterns (such as 'it is all I am not good enough'), lowering the tone, avoiding mention of external support or buffering factors.

manifestations: Feeling trapped in a 'dead-end' Work, believing choices are Restricted
Lacking a sense of control over future financial stability
Withdrawal in social settings involving finance/property topics
Uses others' progress as a reference, weakening the value of one's own choices and path
outcomes: Social avoidance and Increased sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently using absolutist self-evaluations like 'forever / impossible' in sessions
Repeatedly worrying 'it may still not be enough' when setting actions
Focusing more on one's own shortcomings while ignoring existing strengths and resources

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves.
manifestations: Not expressing financial unease to friends/colleagues, bearing Anxiety alone
Avoids finance-related social settings to escape comparison

positive_force: Having Good interpersonal and customer-service skills, having received multiple interview opportunities
Willing to proactively seek change (tries budgeting, applies for higher-paying jobs)
Has a supportive network of friends and colleagues
Willing to seek counseling and able to set small-step action goals
negative_force: Marked catastrophizing, overgeneralizing, and comparative thinking, low Self-efficacy
Making negative predictions about the future (Fortune Telling), reinforcing helplessness
Avoids finance-related social exchanges, reducing external support
External pressure: rising housing prices and costs in the city intensify Anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent anxiety and Catastrophizing about finances and buying a house
antecedent: Noticing rising housing prices / cost of living
Seeing friends or colleagues buying houses or investing in property
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by core beliefs like 'I am not capable enough to earn enough money' and 'the situation cannot change', plus cognitive biases like catastrophizing, predicting the future, and overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control short-term through worrying and repeated evaluation, avoiding facing uncertainty and the Fear of failure
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep impaired, Decline in work performance, intensifying Anxiety and hopelessness

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids social activities involving finance/property topics
antecedent: Gathering / conversation topics involve salary, buying a house, or investment
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being compared and judged, with shame and the self-concept of 'I am inferior'
target_behavior.function: Avoiding being evaluated and the Anxiety and shame triggered by comparison
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, Increased sense of isolation, negative beliefs maintained
